subject: BrightMart post-demo: streaming acceptance criteria & next-step MAP
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@brightmart.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: BrightMart post-demo: streaming acceptance criteria & next-step MAP

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Below is a concise recap of the performance criteria we captured and the proposed MAP (mutual action plan) so we can align on what constitutes an "accept" decision after a short perf validation run. Attaching the SLO checklist and the perf config we discussed.

Summary of targets we took away:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (first-token) <= 250 ms for 512-token payloads (interactive UI flows). For streaming UX, time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target <= 150 ms and stable tail latency (p99) <= 400 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 120 reqs/min (peak bursts to 240r/min) with batch sizes up to 8 for non-streaming workloads.
- Concurrency: up to 80 concurrent active sessions across two regions (US-W & US-E) during campaign spikes.
- Streaming specifics: client expects server-sent events with an initial partial token within the TTFB window and per-chunk latency < 80 ms. We will enable chunked streaming and backpressure handling in the test harness.
- Quality guardrail: identical model variant as demo (redwood-open-1.1-q8) for perf runs; we will also run a small set of evaluation prompts to ensure no regression > 2% on freshness metrics.

Proposed next steps (MAP):
1) BrightMart: share a 48-hr representative production trace or simplified request sample + target SLOs confirmed (Elliot / Priya) — due 2026-11-17.
2) Redwood: provision a short-living test tenant with access token + perf harness; run baseline with our baseline model and provide a report (Rishi) — scheduled 2026-11-19 to 11-20.
3) Joint canary: run a 2-hour canary with live traffic replay and measure latencies, errors, and cost delta — target 2026-11-23.
4) Decision checkpoint: Win criteria = SLOs met for latency & streaming TTFB and acceptable cost per 1k tokens (within BrightMart threshold); plan for dedicated capacity if good (commercial discussion).

Open items / asks for BrightMart:
- Confirm the exact tokenization / average payload size for the UI flows (avg tokens per request).
- Any TLS termination or proxy details (WAF) that will be present in front of our test endpoint.

Attachments: brightmart_slo_checklist_v1.pdf, perf-test-config-512t.json

Thanks — I can hop on a 15m sync tomorrow if you want to walk the checklist.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@brightmart.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightmart.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:01:12 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightMart post-demo: streaming acceptance criteria & next-step MAP

Vanessa — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) The 512-token number is our 95th percentile payload for the conversational UI; average is ~220 tokens. We'll drop you a sanitized trace by EOD Monday.
2) For streaming, we care most about TTFB to visible tokens — if you can show a reproducible <150 ms on your perf run we're happy.
3) Cost: can you provide a ballpark delta between hosted vs. dedicated for this workload (e.g., $/1k tokens) so we can prep budget?

Also, two quick asks:
- Can Rishi include any quantization variants you plan to test? Priya and I would like to see perf vs. quality delta table.
- We want to run the canary with replayed traffic from Nov 3rd campaign (low-PII). I'll upload a sample to the Drive folder you linked.

If this all looks right we'll hold the decision meeting on 2026-11-24 afternoon PT.

Best,
Elliot
Director, Search & Recommendations
BrightMart

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightMart post-demo: streaming acceptance criteria & next-step MAP

Quick internal note / plan before we run the baseline: 

- I'll prepare two baseline configs: (A) fp16 baseline (open-1.1-fp16) and (B) q8 / q4 variants used in the demo. We'll measure token throughput, p50/p95/p99, and first-token TTFB for streaming.
- For streaming TTFB, we'll instrument the harness to report both server enqueue latency and network send latency (client-side). Please ensure the trace you send keeps the timestamping intact.
- We'll run the first pass on a 4xA100 pool to reproduce demo conditions, then on a 2xT4-equivalent profile to model likely dedicated capacity.
- I'll document the perf vs. quality tradeoffs in a single-sheet table (expected by EOD 11/20).

Action items for David: can you pre-seed the perf harness with the perf-test-config-512t.json (attached) and reserve the 4xA100 window on 11/19?

Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
